$comment: New York's HOME CARE AIDE minimum wage -- a separate, higher wage floor set by Public Health Law 3614-f, not the state's ordinary Labor Law 652 rate carried in states/NY-2026.json. This file exists to close a knownGap that file explicitly disclosed: 'NYSDOL publishes it in fact sheet P105, which was not read this pass. No figure is asserted here rather than guessed.' It is stored as a sectoral (occupation-based) file rather than folded into the state file's own variants, the same way California's fast-food and health-care rates are kept separate from its state rate -- 'home care aide' is a statutory job classification, not a geography, and a covered worker is owed this rate regardless of which of New York's two Labor-Law-652 regions they work in.

sectors.name: Home care aides -- New York City, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester counties
sectors.coverage: Public Health Law 3614-f. A 'home care aide' is a home health aide or personal care aide whose primary responsibility is in-home assistance with activities of daily living for a Medicaid-funded or licensed/certified home care services agency, LHCSA or fiscal intermediary client -- narrower than 'anyone who does home care work'; casual/informal caregivers and relatives are excluded by the statute's own definition. Region matches the SAME four downstate counties as Labor Law 652's own 'downstate' region.
sectors.note: $1.00 above the same region's ordinary Labor Law 652 rate of $17.00 -- home care aides are NOT paid the standard minimum wage, and an agency paying the ordinary state rate instead of this one is underpaying by a widening margin every year both schedules step.

sectors.name: Home care aides -- remainder of New York State
sectors.coverage: Public Health Law 3614-f, same occupation test as the downstate figure, applied everywhere outside NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester.
sectors.note: $2.65 above the same region's ordinary Labor Law 652 rate of $16.00 -- a WIDER gap than downstate's, because the home care aide schedule has stepped by a fixed statewide dollar amount each year while the two Labor Law 652 regions diverged from each other on a separate track.

knownGaps: Whether a given worker meets Public Health Law 3614-f's own 'home care aide' definition (as opposed to the ordinary Labor Law 652 minimum wage applying instead) is a legal/statutory determination this file does not model.

Wage parity requirements for Medicaid-funded home care (Public Health Law 3614-c), which layer a benefits component on top of the cash wage in NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester, are a separate and larger obligation not carried here -- this file carries only the Public Health Law 3614-f minimum cash wage.

NY DOL's minimum wage page (read directly 2026-10-01) says the home care aide minimum wage rises on 2027-01-01 to $20.00 per hour in NYC, Long Island and Westchester and $19.00 in the rest of the state (from $19.65 / $18.65), capped at $3.00 above the standard wage. Not applied here: this is a 2026 file and the engine has no 2027 tax year yet.
The FARE (Fair Pay for Home Care) grant program that some agencies rely on to fund this wage is a funding mechanism, not a different wage floor, and is not modelled.

This file was not read against the NYSDOL fact sheet's own primary text this session (see that source's own verifiedBy note) -- only against two independent secondary summaries of it. Re-verify directly when the primary page is reachable.
